MAE I Trust Myself? Self-Evaluating VLA Action Generation with Markov Attention Entropy

Architecture-aware attention entropy turns a VLA’s internal visual addressing into an action-reliability signal.

Aniri

August 17, 2026 ·Preprint ·3-minute read ·Read the paper ·PDF ·Code
1Why this matters 2How it works 3What the study finds 4What this means

The short version

MAE studies whether vision–language–action models can assess their own action generation using internal attention signals. A conditional generative Markov-chain view supplies a common abstraction across latent readout and latent refinement, while the score remains aware of their different computational roles.

That distinction matters: visual concentration associated with reliable readout does not imply that the same entropy orientation is appropriate for iterative refinement. MAE-D and MAE-C use architecture-aware orientations, turning visual addressing into comparable reliability rankings without expert failure labels for score training.

4,000LIBERO-Reflect episodes
3VLA policies evaluated
2 familiesReadout and refinement

A reliability signal must be interpreted in relation to the computation that produces the action.

Why this matters

Output uncertainty provides only a partial view of robotic action generation, especially when policies use different action heads or refinement procedures. Internal signals may contain additional evidence, but a uniform interpretation can erase the architectural differences that give those signals meaning.

How it works

  1. Represent heterogeneous action-generation procedures through a shared conditional latent-transition abstraction.
  2. Extract visual-attention entropy and use the appropriate orientation for latent-readout or latent-refinement policies.
  3. Evaluate reliability rankings on LIBERO-Reflect with standard and challenging episodes across several task subsets.

What the study finds

LIBERO-Reflect contains 4,000 episodes, split evenly between standard and challenging conditions. Evaluations cover OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, and QwenPI-Flow and report AUPR, AUROC, and FPR@95. Ablations compare visual and text heads, selection scope, efficiency, and repeated simulator seeds.

What this means

The work connects self-evaluation to the structure of the computation being evaluated. Attention entropy becomes useful when its direction and location are matched to the action-generation mechanism; the same numerical tendency can mean different things in different architectures.

This offers a route toward monitoring based on existing internal information. A reliability ranking can inform future decisions about intervention or fallback, while threshold calibration and closed-loop benefits require their own evaluation beyond a successful ranking experiment.
